title: Organisational structure
examples: What is the difference between a tall and a flat structure?
How does delegation help a manager?
Can a company have too many levels?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how businesses are organised.
A hierarchy shows the levels of authority in a business.
The span of control is how many people one manager oversees.

draw.text: Span of Control: Manager's Team Size

explain.say: Delegation means passing down tasks to lower levels of staff.
In a large company, delegation helps speed up decision making.
A common mistake is keeping all decisions at the top level.

items: Too much control at the top

faq.q: What is the difference between delegation and passing a task?
faq.a: Delegation is formally giving authority to complete a task. It includes the power to make decisions, not just doing the work.
asks: Is delegation the same as assigning work?
Does delegation mean giving up power?

faq.q: Does a company need a strict hierarchy?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Some modern businesses use flatter structures to encourage faster communication.
asks: Must every business have many levels?

faq.q: What happens if a manager has a very wide span of control?
faq.a: They might become overloaded with too many responsibilities to manage effectively.
asks: What is too wide span of control?
Is it bad to manage many people?

faq.q: How does delayering affect the company?
faq.a: Delayering removes management levels, making communication faster and giving staff more power.
asks: What is the effect of fewer managers?

faq.q: Is it always good to delegate everything?
faq.a: No, some core, sensitive decisions must remain with senior management for consistency.
asks: Should I delegate everything I do?
Are there things I should never delegate?

facts: A hierarchy shows the chain of command in a business.
A wide span of control means managing many people.
Delegation involves transferring authority and responsibility.
Delayering means removing management levels from the structure.

quiz.say: A company has a CEO, then VPs, then Department Heads, and finally staff. This shows a:
quiz.why: The structure shows clear levels of authority from top to bottom.

wrong.1: Span of control measures how many people report to one manager, not the levels themselves.
wrong.2: Delegation is the act of passing down tasks, not the structure itself.
wrong.3: This structure has many levels, making it tall, not flat.

quiz.say: A manager oversees exactly eight team members. This relates to:
quiz.why: Span of control measures the number of subordinates a manager directly supervises.

wrong.0: Delayering is about removing entire levels of management.
wrong.2: Hierarchy describes the layers of management, not the number of people under one person.
wrong.3: Delegation is about giving tasks, not counting the number of people managed.

quiz.say: A senior manager gives a junior employee the authority to approve small purchases up to fifty pounds.
quiz.why: Giving authority and responsibility for a task is the definition of delegation.

wrong.0: This is an action, but delegation specifically refers to transferring authority.
wrong.1: Flattening is a structural change, while this is an action within the structure.
wrong.2: This is a general term for structural change, not the specific act of task transfer.
